title: Unified Osculator Theorem: Merge Positive and Negative Cases

problemStatement.formal: d ∣ n ↔ d ∣ (n/10 + c·(n%10)) for any c with d | (10c-1)
problemStatement.plain: Can the positive and negative osculator theorems be merged into a single theorem with a signed osculator c ∈ ℤ?
whyMatters: Eliminates redundancy between two separate truncation theorems
Shows negative osculator is just the positive case with negated c
Reveals dual osculator structure: c₊ + c₋ ≡ 0 (mod d)

proven: unified_osculator: single theorem for all truncation rules
neg_osculator_from_unified: negative case derived from positive
dual_osculators_sum: c₊ + c₋ divisible by d

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: 159 lines, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Unified osculator theorem merging positive/negative cases into a single statement.
insights: truncation_pos already works with c ∈ ℤ - negative osculator is c := -c_neg
10*(-c) - 1 = -(10c + 1), so dvd_neg.mpr handles the sign change
Dual osculators satisfy d | (c₊ + c₋) via summing the two divisibility conditions

approaches.name: Sign absorption
approaches.description: Use unified_osculator with negative c to derive negative osculator case
